newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China tungsten imports possible, but volumes small.
newsitem.headline: China tungsten imports possible, but volumes small.

text.p: Hong Kong traders could not confirm on Friday market talk that China is currently importing tungsten, but said they were not surprised at the reports despite China's traditional position as a tungsten exporter.
"We looked into a (tungsten import) deal a few months ago, but we found it too risky because of the price volatility, but I can imagine somebody is doing it," said one metals trader.
But the import volumes are likely to be small, he said.
Industry sources said China could be importing small amounts of tungsten because of high domestic prices, which are reported to have risen between 8.0-10 percent in the past few months.
The domestic price of tungsten is currently quoted at about 22,000 yuan a tonne, and at US$5.50/6.00 per kilo on the international market.

Traders said Russian stockpiles of tungsten -- accumulated during the cold war years for use in the defence industry -- had dwindled following the break-up of the Soviet Union and some of that metal had trickled back to China for conversion into ammonium para-tungsten (APT) and re-export.
"A number of conversion contracts have been going on over the last few years, although in recent months it would be much less because there isn't that much left," a senior trader said.
There would be some demand in China as the government had shut down loss-making tungsten factories to focus on a few large ones.
"That creates not a shortage, but the need to import tungsten as a raw material for some of those convertors," the senior trader said.
APT is a tungsten intermediate usually converted to powder and other forms for industrial use.
